leaderboard-hot-topics.name: Hot topic ranking
leaderboard-hot-topics.description: Rank today's / recent hot topics from bound sources with scores and summaries
leaderboard-hot-topics.promptTemplate: Rank today's and recent hot topics from bound sources. Score heat by discussion volume, forwards, and sentiment; merge different phrasings of the same topic; write a one-line summary per topic. Ignore chatter, join-group spam, and system notices. Do not invent topics when nothing is hot enough.

leaderboard-discussion-heat.name: Discussion heat
leaderboard-discussion-heat.description: Rank themes that keep coming up in bound channels by discussion heat
leaderboard-discussion-heat.promptTemplate: Rank themes that are mentioned repeatedly in the channels. Merge different phrasings of the same story into one item, score by mention count and discussion heat, and write a short summary of why it heated up. Ignore one-off chatter and system notices.

key-insights.name: Key intel summary
key-insights.description: Extract high-value intel events and opportunities
key-insights.promptTemplate: Extract high-value intelligence events and leads from the messages. Prioritize: major events, business opportunities, risk alerts, trend shifts. Fill time/location when clear; otherwise keep title and body only.

schedule-events.name: Schedule event extraction
schedule-events.description: Conservative: fill schedule times only when the message states an explicit date/clock time. Do not infer relative phrases like next Wednesday. Best when you want hit-and-record without guessing times.
schedule-events.promptTemplate: Extract schedulable meetings, events, deadlines, and launches. Be conservative on time: fill start_time/end_time only when the message states an explicit date or clock time (e.g. Mar 5 14:00, 2026-07-20). Do not convert relative phrases such as tomorrow / next Wednesday / this Friday (you may still emit the event without time fields). Prefer clear location and participants. Ignore verification flows, join reminders, and system notices.

schedule-time-inference.name: Schedule time inference
schedule-time-inference.description: Inferential: even without a hard-coded calendar date, convert relative phrases (e.g. next Wednesday 6pm, due this Friday, project/event milestones) into schedulable times. Best when you want a filled timeline.
schedule-time-inference.promptTemplate: Infer schedulable itineraries, meetings, activities, project milestones, and deadlines. Unlike explicit-only extraction, convert relative phrases into concrete times when reasonable (e.g. meeting next Wednesday at 6, due this Friday, deliver next month, countdown, milestones). Prefer the message [time=...] stamp as the anchor; otherwise use the injected system clock. Fill start_time/end_time when conversion is sound; if evidence is weak, explain in body and do not invent times. Ignore verification flows, join reminders, and system notices.

crypto-airdrop-deals.name: Airdrop and deal intel
crypto-airdrop-deals.description: Extract airdrops, points quests, testnets, promo codes, and similar opportunities
crypto-airdrop-deals.promptTemplate: Extract Crypto/Web3 monetizable opportunities (airdrops, points, testnets, early access, rebates, whitelist, free mint, quest rewards, etc.). In body include: project/platform, opportunity type, participation conditions and steps, estimated upside if knowable, and risk notes (scam/high gas/unclear rules). Fill start_time when a clear deadline or snapshot exists; prioritize soon-expiring or actionable items. Ignore pure shilling and chatter without concrete steps; omit time fields when unknown.

iot-device-alerts.name: IoT device alerts
iot-device-alerts.description: Extract faults, offline, threshold breaches, and security alerts from MQTT/sensor/device logs
iot-device-alerts.promptTemplate: From IoT/MQTT/sensor/device messages, extract alerts that need attention or action. Prioritize: offline/disconnect, fault codes, threshold breaches (temp/humidity/battery/pressure, etc.), security triggers, comms failure, low battery, emergency stop. In body include: device or topic/site id, alert type, severity (high/medium/low), key values or error codes, suggested action. Fill start_time when the event time is clear; location may be site/floor/zone. Ignore: pure heartbeat/keepalive, routine normal readings, duplicate status with no new info, debug noise. Return empty items when there is no alert.

security-scam-watch.name: Security and scam watch
security-scam-watch.description: Flag phishing, account theft, malware links, vulns, and social engineering
security-scam-watch.promptTemplate: Extract security/scam alerts. Prioritize: phishing links, fake support, account-theft tactics, malware files, known CVE/exploits, social-engineering scripts. In body include: threat type, tactic summary, telltale signs, suggested defenses, severity (high/medium/low). Fill start_time when clear. Ignore jokes and panic forwards with no actionable detail; return empty items when none apply.

policy-regulation.name: Policy and regulation
policy-regulation.description: Track legislation, regulatory notices, enforcement, and compliance deadlines
policy-regulation.promptTemplate: Extract policy/regulatory events. Prioritize: bill progress, agency notices, enforcement/fines, license/permit changes, compliance deadlines. In body include: jurisdiction or agency, topic, status (draft/passed/effective/enforcement), and industry impact. Fill start_time/end_time for clear effective or due dates. Ignore pure political venting without normative content.

finance-markets.name: Finance and markets
finance-markets.description: Capture rates, earnings, commodities, and macro market turns (not crypto-only)
finance-markets.promptTemplate: Extract finance/macro market events. Prioritize: rates/central banks, earnings and guidance, M&A, major commodity/FX moves, regulatory impacts on markets. In body include: market or ticker, event type, key figures or conclusions, likely impact. Fill start_time when clear. Ignore baseless calls and pure sentiment forecasts; use a Crypto template for crypto-specific feeds.

agent-work-shift.name: Work shifts
agent-work-shift.description: Write duty/rotation from bound sources into My schedule; update the same shift when its date changes. No web search.
agent-work-shift.promptTemplate: Write duty, rotation, and shift rosters from bound sources into My schedule. Rules: 1) if the source changes the date of the same person's same shift, update that event instead of creating another; 2) create only when no matching shift exists; 3) cancel/leave means deactivate or delete the matching item; 4) record person, shift, date, and time clearly; 5) do not search the web; 6) ignore unrelated chatter. Finish with a short summary of this turn's changes.

agent-project-schedule.name: Project schedule
agent-project-schedule.description: Write engineering/project milestones in the same workset (e.g. foundation, fit-out) into My schedule; update that event when the source changes the date, or create if none exists. No web search.
agent-project-schedule.promptTemplate: Write engineering/project milestones in the same workset into My schedule, such as foundation, fit-out, inspection, and handover. Rules: 1) if the source changes a date, update that event; create only when unmatched; 2) cancel means deactivate or delete; 3) record only the milestone's date and content — do not claim or invent Gantt dependencies or predecessor/successor links; 4) write only when the date is explicit or reasonably convertible; 5) do not search the web; 6) ignore unrelated chatter. Finish with a short summary of this turn's changes.

agent-source-verify.name: Source verification
agent-source-verify.description: Use bound sources as clues, verify against public news on the web, and write intel events.
agent-source-verify.promptTemplate: Use bound source messages as clues, then verify with web.search against public news. Rules: 1) pull people, orgs, events, or dates from sources as search clues; 2) do not finish without a successful search; if snippets are not enough, web.fetch 1–2 URLs; 3) write only publicly verifiable facts; if the source conflicts with public news, say so in the body; 4) write intel events, not My schedule; 5) ignore chatter and unverifiable rumors. Finish by writing the verified findings as intel events.

agent-pure-web-search.name: Pure web search
agent-pure-web-search.description: No bound sources; scheduled forced web search; write findings as intel events
agent-pure-web-search.promptTemplate: Use web.search on the task topic for the latest public news; do not finish without a successful search. If snippets are not enough, web.fetch 1–2 URLs. Do not rely on Telegram or other bound sources; this template binds no channels. Finish by writing the highlights as intel events.
